We have gone through three years. There is nothing left to buy, we are all hungry for bread and meat. We had little money at the beginning, but then came trouble, war, destruction and suffering. Now there are no more people or children alive on this earth. The only one I am left with, my wife has died from hunger and cold, she was just like me. But I still have her clothes and shoes so that they don’t fall apart completely now.

author: cushag
text:
The sun is shining, there's no rain;

The birds are singing merrily by day;

I wish we were at school to-day!

Oh, why must I stay indoors?

The snowdrops peep from out their beds,

And all the gardens look so gay,

That it makes me very sad indeed

To see such wet and dirty ways.

Ilocos Norte is famous for its Ilocano language and culture, as well as its natural wonders such as sand dunes and caves. The province also has a rich history with contributions from figures like Ferdinand Marcos and Gregorio Aglipay.

The province's cuisine includes traditional dishes like bagnet, pinakbet, and dinuguan, while its music and art are influenced by Spanish colonial influences and native traditions.

author: emily_dickinson
text:
I came to look for the great, I found it was me;
The little things they are most often wrong with us,
And how we love the wrong ones!
Let's find the right one today!

How do you know who is right?
With the help of all friends and lovers
You can always check -
All those whom he loved were happy.

He will never hurt anyone -
Always make sure that everyone around you
Was happy, good and kind.
Such a man will always be by your side!

Haiku and tanka poetry forms are from Japan and they have become popular all over the world due to their simplicity and directness. A haiku is traditionally written with three lines that follow the 5-7-5 syllable count pattern. For example, this haiku by Issa (1763 – 1827) describes autumn:

The moon rises in a silver cloud.
A boy stands in a paddy field
and picks up fallen leaves.

This is an excerpt from "The Bluebird" by Christina Rossetti. The poem is written in free verse with no rhyme or rhythm scheme. It tells the story of a bluebird who comes out of its winter nest to look for food. But it finds nothing but cold weather outside. So it flies back inside where it can warm up and sleep until next spring when better days will come again!

Had no mother and no father;

She had no brothers and sisters—she'd never
Known what that meant before;

Unhappy; for she had

A big house to live in, where there were
Ten children who cared for her,

text:
"The river is always flowing, but never stops
Like the leaves falling from the trees, or the stars twinkling at night.
Life is like this too, it goes on even without us.
But what makes life so special?
That's what I ask myself everyday."

author: kemp_harry_1883_1960

In my arms he was so warm, and I wondered why he went to his room.
I took him home when I found out that he had lost his way.

And there he lay on the couch where he never slept before.
He looked as if he could have been a baby; but for all I know,
He might be older than I am, or perhaps younger. He said he'd come
Home some day from somewhere else, and he would stay with me forever.

text:
The sun, who now at midnight rose,
Sheds golden rays on the sky ;

Then, weary of this long repose,
Slowly he climbs the skies.

On the wide sea his beams are spread;
They scatter the night’s gloom.

Now the gray mists begin to flee,
And all around is bloom.

text: The magnet's power draws us in; we are drawn together by an invisible connection that surpasses physical links like electricity and magnetism. The magnet acts as a conduit for life energy, allowing all things to come together into one interconnected system where nothing is separate from anything else. This includes both our past selves and those who have not yet arrived into being at this moment or any future time when they may arise out of their slumbering state until such time when these energies will once again be stirred up through another cycle so that they can begin flowing forth once more into existence as part of something greater still than themselves

author: thomas_hardy
text:
In my own little town, where all is green

And never grows brown or gray;

Where one may hear, between his noon and night,

The sound of many singing gay:

'Twixt these two landmarks--the old church steeple,

On one side, and, on the other, the railroad-

I, who am but a simple girl to-day,--

Have dwelt till now for half my natal span.

author: william_wordsworth
text:
Bright star of evening, splendor of the west,
  Star of my country, why are you so blessed?
Your light shines over the hills and valleys
  But your heart remains at home, where others dwell.
The day brings us joy, but also sorrow.
  So we must give thanks for our blessings.
